subject: Clarify: aggregation offset for long-context billing and rounding
messages:
From: Julia Hart <julia.hart@brightcart.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: finance@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing question: aggregated context rounding on Mar invoice

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question on the March invoice attached — our finance team flagged a pattern where multiple short streaming calls that get stitched into a single long-context processing event appear to be charged in a way that double-counts rounding at the microcall level.

Example attached: three streaming calls (each ~1.8k tokens) that are contiguous in the same conversation were billed as if each crossed the 2k token bucket individually, even though the runtime collapsed them into one 5.4k context for inference. This created a ~7% delta vs. our expectation after committed-commit discounts.

Can you explain the intended rounding/aggregation policy when calls are merged server-side? Is rounding applied per-request, per-conversation, or after aggregation? Also: how does this interact with committed minimums and the prorated discount bands in our SOW?

We attached: BrightCart_Invoice_Sample_Mar2028.pdf and billing-usage-sample.csv. If this is expected behavior, we need an explanation for our auditors; if it isn't, can you propose a path to reconcile?

Best,
Julia Hart
Procurement Manager, BrightCart
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Hart <julia.hart@brightcart.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-13T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing question: aggregated context rounding on Mar invoice

Hi Julia — thanks for the detailed example and the invoice. I pulled the usage sample and can see the three short streams you mentioned. Two quick notes up front: 1) we never intend to charge customers more than the effective work done; 2) there are a couple of different places rounding can happen (metering client-side, server aggregation, invoice line grouping).

To be concrete, can you confirm whether the three calls were: (a) separate API requests with separate request IDs, or (b) separate chunks of the same streaming session (same conversation_id) that later merged in our runtime? That affects whether aggregation is applied before unitization.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll loop in Vanessa from pricing ops for SOW/commit-band interpretation.
- If you can share the HubSpot deal id (or confirm BRIGHT-3671), I can map discount bands to the invoice programmatically.
- Suggest a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the invoice line-by-line; if we missed applying an aggregation rule we can issue a corrective credit promptly.

I've cc'd Vanessa — she can propose the reconciliation playbook.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-13T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: aggregation + commit bands — reconciliation options

Kim / Sean — quick internal note before we jump on the call with BrightCart. Summary of what I see: the runtime aggregates contiguous KV-prefix calls into a single execution window when conversation_id matches and requests fall within a short time delta (our default is 60s). Metering is implemented in two layers: per-request observation (for real-time quotas) and post-facto unitization (for billing). The invoice pipeline should use the post-facto aggregation, but we've observed edge cases when streaming sessions close and reopen within the heartbeat window — leading to duplicate rounding at the microcall level.

Options to propose to the customer:
- Immediate corrective credit for March equal to the delta once we re-run the unitization on their sample (recommended if re-run shows overcount).
- Policy change: apply rounding after aggregation at conversation level (not per-request) for all accounts on this pilot (affects accounting; needs finance sign-off).
- A pragmatic compromise: one-time 5% invoice credit for March plus a commitment to schedule a billing-pipeline patch in next release; document change in SOW amendment.

I attached SOW_draft_kp_v1.pdf with language for a small amendment to make the aggregation rule explicit. If we go down the credit route, offering a 5% credit is a good sales compromise and keeps the contract tidy; if they push for reprocessing historical months we should tie that to a self-service true-up clause to limit scope.

Thoughts? If approved I'll draft the exact credit figure and the amendment and prepare the DocuSign link.

-Vanessa
Head of Pricing Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Hart <julia.hart@brightcart.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, finance@brightcart.com
Date: 2028-04-14T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing question: aggregated context rounding on Mar invoice

Hi Julia — thanks for raising this and for the example files. We dug into your sample and confirmed that the three calls were separate API requests that our runtime merged into a single execution for inference (same conversation_id and within heartbeat window). The invoice generator incorrectly applied per-request rounding for that batch in one pipeline step — that produced the ~7% delta you observed.

What we'll do:
- We'll re-run unitization against the csv you sent and produce a corrected invoice line for March. If the re-run shows over-counting, we'll issue a corrective credit on next invoice.
- As a commercial gesture while we complete the re-run, Redwood will apply a one-time 5% credit to the March invoice amount (applies regardless of re-run result).
- We'll also provide an updated SOW amendment that clarifies the aggregation policy (link to DocuSign: https://na2.docusign.com/BRIGHTCART_AMENDMENT_3671).

Can you confirm you want Redwood to proceed with the re-run and to accept the 5% credit for March? If yes I'll route the amendment for signature and confirm the exact credit figure from finance (cc'ing Vanessa).

Appreciate the catch — we want to be predictable on economics for you and your auditors.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Lead | Redwood Inference
